call_path_observed.loopback: fabric/loopback/pc_node_server.py::_handle_capability_request() calls wire.safe_capability_request_from_wire(payload) then fi.process_remote_capability_request(request, local_transport, lineage_store=lineage_store, artifact_index=artifact_index) -- the same unmodified function proven at every prior layer.
call_path_observed.tcp: fabric/tcp/pc_node_server.py::_handle_capability_request() has one EXTRA defense-in-depth check (request.capability_id != ALLOWED_CAPABILITY_ID -> CAP_UNSUPPORTED before dispatch) not present in loopback, then calls the identical fi.process_remote_capability_request(...). Both transports share fabric.loopback.wire for serialization verbatim -- fabric/tcp/ imports it directly, does not reimplement it.

loopback.transport_path: fabric.loopback.transport.LoopbackClientTransport (AF_UNIX on this Linux sandbox; AF_PIPE on Windows per make_loopback_address) <-> a genuinely separate OS subprocess (subprocess.Popen) running fabric/loopback/pc_node_server.py unmodified.
loopback.serialization_path: fabric.loopback.wire.capability_request_to_wire()/safe_capability_request_from_wire(), authority_to_wire()/safe_authority_from_wire() -- plain JSON over multiprocessing.connection's own message framing (one send_bytes() = one message).
loopback.expired_executor_invocations: 0, proven via the server subprocess's own on-disk LineageStore: 0 records after the denied request (ah_interface.handoff(), which writes lineage, only runs after authority_permits() succeeds, strictly before provider.invoke()).
loopback.future_result: CAP_COMPLETED, structured_result['text_content'] equals the exact real payload sent (fabric.tests.test_authority_expiry_loopback.TestFutureAuthorityOverLoopback). LineageStore shows exactly 1 record matching the artifact's sha256 -- direct evidence of exactly one real content_read execution.
loopback.none_result: CAP_COMPLETED, structured_result content verified identical to pre-expiry-enforcement behavior (fabric.tests.test_authority_expiry_loopback.TestNoneExpiryOverLoopback).
loopback.malformed_result: CAP_UNAUTHORIZED, 0 lineage records (fabric.tests.test_authority_expiry_loopback.TestMalformedExpiryOverLoopback). A malformed expires_at string ('not-a-timestamp') survives JSON serialization unmutated (proven directly by TestAuthorityWireRoundTripPreservesGovernanceFields::test_malformed_expiry_string_survives_round_trip_unmutated) and reaches the real server process exactly as constructed -- not a synthetic bypass.
loopback.authority_roundtrip_result: PROVEN at the pure wire layer (no subprocess needed to isolate this step): actor_id, granted_capability_ids, granted_by, and expires_at (including a past timestamp, None, and a malformed string) all survive wire.authority_to_wire() -> json.dumps() -> json.loads() -> wire.safe_authority_from_wire() byte-for-byte / value-for-value identical to the original. 3/3 tests pass.
loopback.also_verified: future expiry does not bypass the pre-existing capability allowlist check: a future (non-expired) grant for a DIFFERENT capability_id than requested is still CAP_UNAUTHORIZED with 0 lineage writes (TestExpiryDoesNotWeakenAllowlistOverLoopback).

full_regression_result.run_method: python3 -m unittest <module>, one suite per subprocess, this session, in the mission-specified order
full_regression_result.baseline_comparison: Prior evidence-backed baseline was 168/168. This run reproduces all 168 unchanged plus 13 new transport-governance tests = 181, zero regressions, zero unexplained failures.
full_regression_result.unrunnable_reason: pytest not installed in this sandbox; unchanged from all prior missions

counterevidence: None. Both transports enforce the identical governance rule identically, because both dispatch into the identical unmodified process_remote_capability_request() and share the identical unmodified wire serialization module. No defect found in either transport.
limitations: Exact-boundary (evaluation_time == expires_at) is not re-proven at the transport layer -- neither pc_node_server.py exposes a clock-injection seam, and adding one would be a production modification outside this mission's preferred zero-change outcome. It remains proven only at the authority_permits() unit layer (fabric/tests/test_authority_expiry.py::TestExactBoundaryIsRejected).

The TCP proof is loopback-bound (127.0.0.1) in this sandbox only. No physical Android/Termux phone was involved and no LAN interface was exercised. FW-FABRIC-DEVICE-BOUNDARY-001's own prior evidence already documents that fabric/tcp/ has never been exercised on real Windows or against a physical device.

The lineage-store-based zero-execution proxy proves 'authority passed and handoff() was reached', one step short of literally instrumenting provider.invoke() itself. Combined with the structured_result content check (which can only be produced by content_read's real invoke() actually running), this is treated as equivalent-strength evidence to the in-process spy counter used in FW-AUTHORITY-EXPIRY-E2E-001, but it is not a byte-identical invocation counter -- recorded as a methodological difference, not a gap in the conclusion.

TCP's authority-roundtrip was not independently re-tested under a separate filename since it reuses the identical fabric.loopback.wire module the loopback file already tests directly; this is a deliberate non-duplication, not an oversight.
newly_discovered_gaps: No message identity/nonce, replay protection, cryptographic integrity, peer identity proof beyond the shared multiprocessing.connection authkey challenge, sequence/order guarantees, idempotency, duplicate suppression, transport-level encryption, or capability-receipt correlation beyond correlation_id/causation_id exist in either transport. These are pre-existing architectural gaps (consistent with architecture/transport-map.md and architecture/sentinel-map.md's prior observations), not introduced or worsened by this mission, and are recorded here per Section 14 for the later phone<->PC trust-boundary microphases -- not repaired under this authorization.
